newsitem.title: USA: Military contractors settle U.S. government disputes.
newsitem.headline: Military contractors settle U.S. government disputes.

text.p: Two military contractors agreed to pay the U.S. government a total of $16.8 million to settle separate allegations of fraud, overcharging and failure to meet defense contract conditions, the Justice Department announced on Monday.
Teledyne Industries Inc., a unit of Allegheny Teledyne, will pay the government $11.5 million to settle two disputes, the department said in a written statement.
The first case, settled for $4.75 million, involved allegations that Teledyne defrauded the government by failing to account for aircraft engine parts used to repair Air Force jets at 15 bases.
The other $6.75 million payment settled a claim that its Teledyne Thermatics failed to properly test wire and cable as required by its defense contract, the statement said.

The Department also announced that Lockheed Martin Inc. (LMT.N) had agreed to pay the government $5.3 million to settle allegations it overcharged the Pentagon on a contract to develop a supersonic, low-altitude target for missiles.
The settlement resolved charges brought against the Martin Marietta Corporation, now Lockheed Martin Inc., by former employee Jerry Mayman.
Mayman alleged that the company overcharged the Pentagon by bidding low to win the contract and then making up the shortfall by boosting costs.

The Justice Department, intervening in the case, alleged in its complaint that Martin Marietta knowingly underbid the contract and then recovered contract costs by charging them to research and development, which was reimbursed by the government.
Under the settlement, Mayman would receive $790,000 for bringing the matter to the attention of the government, the statement said.

The False Claims Act, under which the case was brought, allows a private party to file an action on behalf of the United States and receive a portion of the settlement if the government takes over the case and prosecutes it successfully.
